title: Effectivity of the primitive completion maps
statement: Fix l, E and an Operations record [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. Let each integral input be finite-Tor bounded constructible and derived complete [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], or equal to the scalar tensor unit. Then tensorCompletion at any pair of such inputs is an isomorphism. For every separated locally finite-type quasi-compact scheme morphism, the specified ordinary-to-completed pullback unit at such an input is an isomorphism. The actual reduction/total-limit adjunction unit at such an input is an isomorphism as well. All maps are the specified ambient maps; no word or recursive completion map occurs in the conclusion.

proof.text: For two finite-Tor constructible inputs, apply lem-sf-finite-tor-ordinary-tensor-complete to the ordinary tensor of the fixed calculus. If either input is the scalar unit, its left or right unitor identifies that ordinary tensor with the other complete input. Completeness of the scalar tensor unit is the proved tensorUnit_complete helper in OpenReconstructionEffectivity. RingedModels.tensorClosed identifies the ordinary tensor of the supplied normalized presentation with this fixed tensor. Roos/intrinsic completeness equivalence makes its actual quotient completion unit invertible, and composition with Tensor.comparison proves invertibility of the specified tensorCompletion map.

Apply lem-sf-finite-tor-ordinary-pull-complete to the ordinary ringed pullback of either allowed kind of input. Roos/intrinsic completeness equivalence makes the actual quotient completion unit at this object invertible. Pull.unit is this unit followed by the normalized Pull.comparison isomorphism, so it is invertible.

A finite-Tor constructible input is complete by its first conjunct and the intrinsic/legacy tower comparison. The scalar tensor unit is complete by the existing tensorUnit_complete proof in OpenReconstructionEffectivity. Apply purNormalizedReconstructionOfScheme to the fixed evaluation calculus: its actual reduction/total-limit adjunction unit is invertible at every complete input, without any geometric invertibility hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Primitive tensor and pullback completeness, followed by the specified quotient units; reconstruction uses purNormalizedReconstructionOfScheme.

theorem primitiveCompletionEffectivity (o : Operations l E) :
    (∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
      (K L : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)),
      (finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X K ∨
        K = (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).integralClosed.monoidal.tensorUnit) →
      (finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X L ∨
        L = (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).integralClosed.monoidal.tensorUnit) →
      IsIso ((tensorCompletion l E o X).app (K, L))) ∧
    (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      IsSeparated f → LocallyOfFiniteType f → QuasiCompact f →
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E Y),
      (finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E Y K ∨
        K = (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E Y).integralClosed.monoidal.tensorUnit) →
      IsIso (((o.ringed.pull f).unit l E).app K)) ∧
    (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)),
      (finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X K ∨
        K = (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).integralClosed.monoidal.tensorUnit) →
      IsIso ((IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).adjunction.unit.app K))
